key_insight: Sizing energy devices for closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts delivers greater average cost savings as forecast error increases, shifting investment from batteries toward photovoltaics and thermal storage.
engineering_relevance: Energy-system planners should account for forecast-driven control when sizing solar generation and storage rather than assume perfect foresight.
method: Formulate device sizing and closed-loop operation as a bi-level optimization problem.
Use backpropagation MPC with a deterministic MPC controller to optimize device sizes.
Generate forecast errors with a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution.
evidence_signal: A case study combining photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage under uncertain weather and demand found increasing benefits from operation-aware sizing as forecast errors grew.
watch_item: The abstract reports one system case study; generalization to other configurations and real-world forecast errors remains to be established.
paper_title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
